remedies.title: Mediterranean Table Tradition
instructions: Cook with olive oil instead of butter or hard fats.
Build meals around vegetables, beans, and whole grains, with meat as a side rather than the centre.
Eat fish a couple of times a week; keep red meat occasional.
Finish meals with fruit rather than sweets.
Eat with others when you can — the shared table is part of the tradition.
remedies.origin: The everyday eating pattern of Crete, southern Italy, and coastal Spain as documented in the mid-20th century.
remedies.disclaimer: A dietary pattern, not a treatment. Adapt with a doctor or dietitian if you have a medical condition.

remedies.title: Daily Fermented Foods
instructions: Add one small serving of a fermented food to a meal each day.
Rotate between dairy, vegetable, and grain ferments through the week.
Choose raw, unpasteurised ferments where safe and available — heat kills the live cultures.
Introduce slowly if you are not used to them.
remedies.origin: Nearly every food culture keeps a ferment: kimchi in Korea, sauerkraut in Central Europe, ogi in Nigeria, laban across the Levant.
remedies.disclaimer: People with weakened immune systems should ask a doctor before eating unpasteurised ferments.

remedies.title: Bitter Greens Before Meals

ingredients.name: bitter leaves (arugula, dandelion, endive, or African bitterleaf, well prepared)

instructions: Start the main meal with a small salad of bitter greens dressed simply with oil and lemon.
Chew slowly — the bitter taste itself triggers digestive juices.
Make it a habit at your largest meal of the day.
remedies.origin: From Italian 'amaro' aperitifs to Nigerian bitterleaf soup, traditions worldwide open digestion with bitterness.
remedies.disclaimer: Wild-foraged greens must be identified with certainty; when in doubt, use market greens.

remedies.title: Eat-the-Rainbow Plate

ingredients.name: vegetables and fruits of at least 4 different colours

instructions: At each main meal, glance at your plate and count the natural colours.
Aim for four or more colours across the day: leafy green, red/orange, purple/blue, white/yellow.
Shop seasonally — colour variety follows the seasons in traditional markets.
remedies.origin: A modern phrasing of an old market-day instinct: a colourful basket is a nourishing basket.
remedies.disclaimer: General guidance, not a treatment plan.

remedies.title: Hara Hachi Bu — Eating to Eight Parts Full

ingredients.name: vegetables, sweet potato, tofu and soup

instructions: Serve into small bowls rather than one large plate, and don't refill automatically.
Eat slowly and put the utensils down between bites.
Stop when you feel about eighty percent full — comfortable, not stuffed.
Wait twenty minutes before deciding you want more; fullness catches up late.
remedies.origin: A Confucian-rooted phrase spoken before meals in Okinawa, where it is credited as part of an unusually long-lived food culture.
remedies.disclaimer: Not appropriate for children, pregnant women, anyone underweight, or anyone with a history of disordered eating.

remedies.title: The Six Tastes at Every Meal
instructions: Aim to include something from each of the six tastes in a main meal — a squeeze of lemon, a pinch of salt, a bitter green, a spiced dal.
Traditionally the meal opens with sweet and finishes with the lighter, astringent tastes.
Notice which tastes you habitually skip; those are usually the ones the cravings point at.
remedies.origin: The shadrasa of classical Ayurveda, still the organising idea behind a traditional Indian thali.
remedies.disclaimer: A framework for composing meals, not a treatment for any condition.

remedies.title: Drinking Around the Meal, Not During It
instructions: Drink a full glass of water about half an hour before the meal.
Sip only small amounts with the food itself.
Wait until the meal has settled, then finish with a warm herbal tea rather than a cold drink.
Keep cold water for between meals, not with them.
remedies.origin: Common practice across Ayurvedic and Mediterranean households alike, where cold drinks at the table are thought to dampen digestion.
remedies.disclaimer: If you take medication with meals, keep taking it as your doctor directed.

remedies.title: Eating with the Season

ingredients.name: whatever the local market has most of, cheapest, that week

instructions: Shop the produce that is piled highest and priced lowest — that is what is in season locally.
Lean on cooling, watery foods in the hot months and slow-cooked, warming ones in the cold.
Preserve a little of a glut — dry, ferment, or freeze it — the way a household with no supermarket would.
Let the plate change four times a year rather than staying identical.
remedies.origin: Not a diet so much as the default condition of eating before year-round shipping — still the backbone of Japanese shun and Mediterranean market cooking.
remedies.disclaimer: General guidance. Nutritional needs in pregnancy or illness may not follow the season.
